quizzes.q: On which date is International Mother Language Day observed?
quizzes.explain: 21 February remembers the 1952 Language Movement. UNESCO proclaimed it International Mother Language Day in 1999.

quizzes.q: How many administrative divisions does Bangladesh have?
quizzes.explain: Bangladesh has 8 divisions; Mymensingh became the eighth in 2015.

quizzes.q: How many districts (zila) does Bangladesh have?
quizzes.explain: Bangladesh has 64 districts across its 8 divisions.

quizzes.q: Which is the largest mangrove forest shared by Bangladesh and India?
quizzes.explain: The Sundarbans, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is often described as the largest mangrove forest in the world.

quizzes.q: Who wrote the words of 'Amar Shonar Bangla', the national anthem of Bangladesh?
quizzes.explain: Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Amar Shonar Bangla'; the first ten lines are the national anthem.

quizzes.q: Who is the national poet of Bangladesh?
quizzes.explain: Kazi Nazrul Islam, the 'rebel poet', is the national poet of Bangladesh.

quizzes.q: Which date is celebrated as Victory Day in Bangladesh?
quizzes.explain: 16 December 1971 marks the end of the Liberation War.

quizzes.q: On which date was the Constitution of Bangladesh adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
quizzes.explain: It was adopted on 4 November 1972 and came into effect on 16 December 1972.

quizzes.q: What is the national fish of Bangladesh?
quizzes.explain: The hilsa, called ilish in Bangla, is the national fish.

quizzes.q: On which date does Pohela Boishakh fall in Bangladesh?
quizzes.explain: Under the revised Bangla calendar used in Bangladesh, 1 Boishakh is 14 April.

quizzes.q: Muhammad Yunus shared the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize with which institution?
quizzes.explain: The prize was awarded jointly to Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank for microcredit.

quizzes.q: In 1610 which city became the provincial capital of Mughal Bengal?
quizzes.explain: Islam Khan I made Dhaka the capital of Mughal Bengal in 1610.

quizzes.q: In which year was the Battle of Plassey fought?
quizzes.explain: At Plassey in 1757 the East India Company defeated the Nawab of Bengal.

quizzes.q: Which Viceroy partitioned Bengal in 1905?
quizzes.explain: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905; the partition was annulled in 1911.

quizzes.q: Which ancient Buddhist monastery at Paharpur is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
quizzes.explain: Somapura Mahavihara in Naogaon was built in the 8th century under the Pala king Dharmapala.

quizzes.q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
quizzes.explain: The Pacific Ocean covers more area than all the land on Earth.

quizzes.q: What is the capital of Japan?
quizzes.explain: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

quizzes.q: Which is the largest continent by area?
quizzes.explain: Asia is the largest continent by both area and population.

quizzes.q: In which year was the United Nations founded?
quizzes.explain: The UN came into being in October 1945 after the Second World War.

quizzes.q: Who was the first human to travel into space?
quizzes.explain: Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth on 12 April 1961.

quizzes.q: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in which field?
quizzes.explain: Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, the first non-European laureate.

quizzes.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
quizzes.explain: Au comes from the Latin word 'aurum'.

quizzes.q: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
quizzes.explain: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

quizzes.q: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
quizzes.explain: Plants use carbon dioxide, water and sunlight to make sugars and release oxygen.

quizzes.q: Approximately how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
quizzes.explain: Light travels at about 299,792 km per second.

quizzes.q: What does the 'H' in HTML stand for?
quizzes.explain: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.

quizzes.q: Which is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
quizzes.explain: Diamond is the hardest known natural material on the Mohs scale.

quizzes.q: What is the smallest prime number?
quizzes.explain: 2 is the smallest prime number and the only even prime.
